data.name: Mostafa
data.gender_notes: Mostafa is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'safa', meaning 'to choose', 'to prefer'. Mostafa is the one who is well-chosen or well-pleased. It is also the name of an important figure in Islamic history, Prophet Moses' servant, Mosa ibn Qatadah. The name Mostafa carries the meaning “Well-chosen, well-pleased” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mostafa usually hope their child will grow to embody well-chosen, well-pleased and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mostafa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Well-chosen, well-pleased.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mostafa total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Mostafa was the name of the first Abbasid caliph, Al-Saffah (r. 750-754 CE). The name 'Mostafa' means 'chosen one' or 'the one approved' in Arabic, which reflects the belief that the caliph was chosen by God to lead the Islamic community.
historical_references.context: The Abbasid Caliphate was a major political and cultural power in the Islamic world, succeeding the Umayyad Caliphate. Al-Saffah's reign marked the beginning of the Abbasid period and the shift of power from Damascus to Baghdad.

historical_references.reference: Mostafa is also the name of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib (r.a., 601-61 CE). The name 'Mostafa' is mentioned in the Quran as a title given to Prophet Ibrahim (pbuh) and his son Isma'il (pbuh), meaning 'submitted to God'. Ali, being a close companion and the fourth caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, carried this title in honour of his devotion to the Prophet and the Islamic community.
historical_references.context: Ali ibn Abi Talib was one of the earliest converts to Islam and a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. He played a crucial role in the early Islamic community and was known for his courage, wisdom, and justice.
